Årsrapport 2023 is the official annual quality report published by the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), a national quality database operating under the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP). Published on 28 November 2023, the report documents the quality of treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation in Denmark during the period from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023 [^src1]. It is primarily targeted at healthcare professionals and political decision-makers, providing conclusions, indicator results, and recommendations that directly influence clinical practice and health policy in Denmark.

The report's findings are built upon registry data from the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] [^src1]. It evaluates both process indicators, such as the time to anticoagulation, and outcome indicators, like the incidence of stroke. Notably, the 2023 edition introduces new data sources, including submissions from private practicing cardiologists and test data from general practice. While the report highlights progress in treatment quality, it also identifies persistent challenges, such as regional variations in care and a lack of structured patient education. Epidemiologically, the report identifies a total of 19,671 incident patients and 134,810 prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation during the covered period [^src1]. 

For inquiries regarding the report, [[julie-andersen|Julie Andersen]], a quality consultant at RKKP, serves as the official contact person [^src1].
